When you have to use a "sound guy" from the local area, still have your own guy in the booth for input; although they will know the rooms acoustics better, the local tech does not know each bands idiosyncrasies and can make a better mix knowing issues ahead of time.

It's quite an art form and I can do sound - and have done sound. However, I'm not a audio engineer and I can't do it nearly as well as someone who has dedicated their time to mastering it. I play my guitar. I trust (and that's not always easy for people) the sound guys to do a good job.

That really is one of the hardest things (concerning this subject) that I see people struggle with. You have to trust your sound guy. You hired them to do a job. You hired them because they're good. If they're not good, don't hire them. Trust them, get out of the way so that they can do their job, and follow their instructions to the letter.

They really can make or break a show. They can take a mediocre set and make it amazing. They can also take an awesome set and turn it to shit. So, find a good one and reward them handsomely.

I absolutely stand by your suggestion of having your own guy in the booth. Even if nothing else, it's the chance for your guy to learn from the guy who knows the venue.
